newsitem.title: FRANCE: Car bomb in Algiers, many feared dead - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Car bomb in Algiers, many feared dead - witnesses.

text.p: A car bomb exploded near a coffee shop in central Algiers on Monday and many people were feared dead, eyewitnesses said.
The bomb went off at about 12.45 a.m. (1145 GMT) in a street near a crowded coffee shop, said the witnesses, speaking by telephone from Algiers.
"I saw much blood at the scene. I fear many people might have died," one witness said.
There was no immediate word on who was responsible for the blast.
Algerian government forces have been locked in conflict for nearly five years with Moslem guerrillas trying to topple the North African country's secular leaders.
About 60,000 people, most of them Moslem militants and security forces members, have died since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election which radical Islamists were set to win.
